synopsis: SCVC regularizes a joint video-action denoiser to agree across camera views only on actions, future proprioception, and value; each future image retains its own camera-dependent supervision. [E02, E03] Its strongest evidence is improved simulated control at viewpoints beyond the training envelope, compared with an identically pair-trained control. Interpolation does not improve and significantly regresses in the second seed. [E12, E13] Controlled experiments support the predicted damage from forcing future images to agree, while a wrist-camera audit exposes a confound in camera-robustness evaluation. [E06, E10]

problem.text: A WAM predicts outputs with different transformation laws: changing the camera should change the future scene image but preserve base-frame actions and other physical targets. Uniform consistency therefore conflicts with correct video supervision. Evaluation must also distinguish benefits from camera exposure, the added consistency objective, and access to a stable wrist view.

contributions.text: The authors propose output-selective consistency and justify both coordinate selection and shared diffusion noise analytically, with controlled verification of the wrong-coordinate shrinkage law.

A carved camera-training distribution separates distribution-matched evaluation, unseen interpolation, and unseen extrapolation. An otherwise matched zero-consistency control isolates the objective from pair exposure.
The masking audit shows that substantial camera-track success can persist without the perturbed scene-camera input, motivating scene-only mechanism experiments.

inputs: Deployment: current scene image o, proprioception q, and language instruction ℓ. [E02]
Training: nominal and perturbed observations rendered from the same recorded physical state, with shared action, future-proprioception, and value labels and camera-specific future images. [E02, E07]
outputs: An action chunk of K = 16 base-frame delta end-effector commands, future proprioception, and value. [E02]
A future scene image corresponding to the conditioning camera. [E02]

steps.name: Establish action-equivalent pairs
steps.detail: Render the same state under two cameras. Shared labels are valid only when actions use the robot base frame, both views remain task-informative, and camera changes preserve task semantics. The authors report checking the action convention against the controller and asserting identical invariant targets during training.

steps.name: Jointly encode prediction targets
steps.detail: The scene-only Cosmos sequence contains seven latent frames: blank, current proprioception, current scene conditioning, actions, future proprioception, future scene, and value. Both training branches use the same denoiser parameters.

steps.name: Apply selective consistency
steps.detail: Share the noise level and realization across branches. Supervise both complete predictions, but penalize their difference only on action, future-proprioception, and value frames. Future-scene predictions remain separately supervised.

training.text: Consistency ramps linearly to λCV = 2.0 during the first 2% of training and applies only to demonstration samples. Rollout-mode samples remain single-view. The integrated manifest contains 583,648 same-state pairs.

Both comparison arms initialize from a nominally trained scene-only Cosmos Policy reference. Each receives 10,000 steps, effective batch 720, 7.2 million sample presentations, learning rate 5 × 10^-5, and EMA; evaluation uses the final checkpoint. The control retains both supervised branches with λCV = 0.

inference.text: SCVC leaves the deployment interface unchanged: one scene observation, proprioception, and instruction condition the joint denoiser. Pairing exists only during training; no camera metadata, depth, or additional view-generation procedure is required by the policy.

Actions are directly predicted within the joint target, and the reported success rates come from closed-loop simulator evaluation. The paper does not specify the executed fraction of each chunk, denoising-step count, or inference-time use of the value output.

equations.explanation: Equation (1): D_v predicts the clean target x_v for view v; w is the denoising weight and Π_I selects invariant frames. Setting λ to zero preserves identical pair exposure.

With D̄ = (D_0+D_p)/2 and δ = (D_0−D_p)/2, consistency increases the penalty on cross-view residuals without changing the mean-target term. The identity also shows that supervision already penalizes residuals at unit weight.

For unequal camera-dependent targets, the pointwise quadratic optimum shrinks legitimate view differences. This establishes bias in the simplified objective, not an exact full-network performance law.

At fixed σ, independent noise adds a covariance term. Under exact view invariance this becomes twice the noise-dependent prediction variance, penalizing legitimate denoising dependence. Away from invariance, its sign is not guaranteed.

results.setting: Scene-only LIBERO-Plus; |h| in (62,75] degrees; 100 tasks, ten trials per task; matched training arms.
results.metric: Closed-loop success and paired task-bootstrap difference
results.value: First seed: SCVC 76.0%; improvement +12.20 percentage points, 95% CI [7.40,17.00]. Second seed: +15.50 points [11.70,19.40].
results.interpretation: Both seeds support extrapolation improvement attributable to the added objective under this controlled protocol.

results.setting: Azimuth hole (20,30) degrees in absolute magnitude; 49 tasks, ten trials per task.
results.metric: Closed-loop success and paired task-bootstrap difference
results.value: First seed: SCVC 85.1%, difference −1.22 points [−4.29,1.84]. Second seed: 85.7%, difference −4.29 points [−7.56,−1.22].
results.interpretation: The first comparison is inconclusive; the second shows a regression. Describing interpolation as uniformly preserved overstates the evidence.

results.setting: Scale in (175,200]; 99 tasks, ten trials per task; secondary endpoint.
results.metric: Closed-loop success and paired task-bootstrap difference
results.value: First seed: SCVC 71.2%, +4.24 points [0.71,7.88]. Second-seed difference: +4.44 points [0.61,8.49].
results.interpretation: A smaller extrapolation benefit replicates across seeds.

results.setting: Official elevation 15, with training at the off-benchmark value 8; 386 tasks, ten trials per task.
results.metric: Closed-loop success and paired task-bootstrap difference
results.value: First seed: SCVC 63.7%, +8.76 points [6.40,11.11]. Second-seed difference: +4.84 points [3.11,6.58].
results.interpretation: Positive effects replicate, but this axis tests only one extrapolated elevation and has no reported interpolation counterpart.

results.setting: Four LIBERO suites, 500 episodes per suite.
results.value: First seed: SCVC 91.7%, difference −0.60 points. Second-seed difference: −0.2 points.
results.interpretation: Aggregate nominal competence changes little; no confidence interval is supplied for this comparison.

results.setting: Synthetic shared-trunk denoiser trained to convergence; separate short 2B WAM diagnostic.
results.value: Synthetic ratios at λ = 0.1, 0.5, 2.0: 0.715, 0.337, 0.116. The wrong-coordinate 2B arm reaches a future-scene ratio of 0.18 after 2,000 steps.
results.comparison: Analytic ratios: 0.714, 0.333, 0.111. Selective and zero-consistency 2B arms remain near 0.98.
results.interpretation: Controlled results closely follow the shrinkage prediction. The short full-model diagnostic supports collapse of view-specific content, but does not measure converged full-scale shrinkage or executed-action degradation.

results.setting: Released wrist-enabled Cosmos policy on camera-perturbed tasks; 1,200 rollouts per condition.
results.value: Scene blacked: 66.6%; scene replaced by noise: 69.7%; wrist blacked: 0.2%.
results.interpretation: Success without the scene view establishes that many tasks can bypass the perturbed sensor. Wrist-mask failure alone cannot distinguish reliance from corruption sensitivity. Table I reports a separate 79.5% camera aggregate, which should not be substituted for this audit baseline.

results.setting: Frozen scene-only reference across orbital severity levels on the camera track.
results.metric: Action success and relative camera-conditioned excess-FID
results.value: Action success falls from 53% to 3%, while relative excess-FID stays between −0.07 and +0.16.
results.comparison: The fidelity diagnostic subtracts an oracle floor from ground-truth replays under the same camera.
results.interpretation: Distributional frame fidelity can remain stable while control fails. This diagnostic neither establishes semantic plan correctness nor constitutes robot-execution success.

limitations.text: All WAM execution evidence is simulated and scene-only. Consistency is trained on demonstration states, leaving failure/recovery states and wrist-camera pose perturbations untested. Real deployment also requires obtaining sufficiently matched cross-view training observations.

Aggregate gains hide substantial heterogeneity: the discussion reports +40.8 points for spatial tasks but −11.6 for object tasks within primary extrapolation, and −40.4 for object tasks under an extreme compound shift. The proposed grasp-precision explanation is an interpretation rather than an isolated causal result.

Two seeds provide limited training-variation evidence, and paired task-bootstrap intervals do not capture that variation. The significant second-seed interpolation regression qualifies the conclusion's preservation language; endpoint interpolation and extrapolation also show no clear benefit.

The pointwise theorem and synthetic convergence experiment do not establish exact shrinkage in the deployed 2B model. The paper supplies neither a converged full-scale wrong-coordinate control nor a direct shared-versus-independent-noise execution ablation.

reproduction.text: Reproduction needs the Cosmos Policy LIBERO checkpoint, nominal scene-only initialization, recoverable demonstration states, and camera-specific future targets. Manifest guards must enforce the disclosed azimuth and scale holes, endpoint training values {±3,±5,±7}, elevation 8, and held-out official evaluation settings.

The supplied text leaves hardware, wall-clock cost, EMA decay, detailed optimizer settings, sampling steps, and action-replanning cadence unspecified. It promises a code/tooling release without supplying a concrete repository. Its shuffled-pair and real-robot corroboration references another work whose bibliography identifier remains the placeholder 2608.XXXXX.

A small mechanism test should repeat the synthetic invariant/covariant experiment with selective and wrong-coordinate penalties, then vary shared versus independent noise while holding targets and optimization fixed. Successful toy verification would still require a separate matched simulator-control test to establish action benefits.

reasoning.text: The architecture supports One Model × Joint prediction: one denoiser directly predicts action, proprioception, future-image, and value frames in a shared latent sequence. The paired branches share parameters and are a training construction. SCVC introduces neither a separate inverse-dynamics model nor an inference-time controller. The multiview subcategory is supported by paired camera observations, but should not imply an explicit 3D representation, reconstruction system, or camera-conditioned deployment.

discussionQuestions: Does SCVC principally help unseen geometry, or difficult viewpoints with performance headroom? The trained azimuth bucket also improves. [E12, E15]
How should consistency respond when occlusion makes one view less informative or physical-state matching is approximate? [E02, E17]
Can task-conditioned consistency preserve the spatial-task gains while preventing object-task regressions under compound camera shifts? [E16]

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, title, author block, and arXiv footer
evidence.detail: Title, four authors, and identifier match the catalog. The supplied artifact identifies itself as arXiv:2608.21402v1, dated 7 August 2026.

evidence.location: PDF p. 3, Section III, including Assumption 1
evidence.detail: Defines same-state camera pairs, invariant actions/proprioception/value, camera-dependent future scenes, the seven-frame sequence, K = 16, and the base-frame action convention with visibility and semantic assumptions.

evidence.location: PDF p. 3, Section IV-A, Eq. (1) and following paragraph
evidence.detail: Both branches receive supervised denoising loss under shared noise. Consistency selects invariant frames, ramps to 2.0 over 2% of training, applies only to demonstrations, and leaves deployment inputs unchanged.

evidence.location: PDF p. 4, Section IV-B, Lemma 1 and Proposition 1 with proofs
evidence.detail: The loss separates into mean error and a residual penalty weighted by 1+4λ. Unequal targets yield optimal prediction differences reduced by 1/(1+4λ).

evidence.location: PDF p. 4, Section IV-B, Proposition 2 and proof
evidence.detail: Independent noise adds twice the cross-covariance trace; at exact invariance this becomes twice the prediction-variance trace. The authors explicitly restrict the positive-sign conclusion.

Synthetic measured ratios are 0.715/0.337/0.116 versus 0.714/0.333/0.111 predictions. At 2,000 steps the 2B wrong-coordinate future-scene guard reaches 0.18 versus approximately 0.98 for selective/control runs; full-scale quantitative verification is deferred.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 4–5, Sections V-A and V-B
evidence.detail: Training uses 583,648 same-state pairs with explicit azimuth/scale holes and extrapolation bounds; sparse endpoint/elevation training values exclude official held-out settings. Evaluation uses fresh benchmark rollouts rather than training demonstrations.

Comparison arms share the carved manifest, initialization, and budget and differ in consistency weight. Orbital interpolation/extrapolation are designated primary endpoints with paired task-bootstrap 95% intervals.

Describes Cosmos initialization, nominal scene-only reference, 10,000 steps, effective batch 720, 7.2 million presentations, learning rate 5×10^-5, EMA, final checkpoints, ten trials per task, and 500 episodes per nominal suite.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Section VI-B; PDF p. 6, Table I
evidence.detail: The 1,200-rollout masking conditions score 80.5% unmasked, 66.6% scene-black, 69.7% scene-noise, and 0.2% wrist-black. Table I separately gives released-policy ID/camera success of 98.5/79.5 and scene-only success of 93.2/26.0.

Orbital severity lowers action success from 53% to 3% while relative excess-FID remains between −0.07 and +0.16. The metric subtracts a camera-matched replay floor and measures distributional fidelity rather than semantic plan correctness.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table II, C2 azimuth interpolation and extrapolation rows
evidence.detail: Interpolation: 49 tasks, control/SCVC 86.3/85.1, difference −1.22 [−4.29,1.84]. Extrapolation: 100 tasks, 63.8/76.0, difference +12.20 [7.40,17.00].

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Section VI-D, second-seed paragraph
evidence.detail: Second-seed differences are orbital extrapolation +15.50 [11.70,19.40], dolly +4.44 [0.61,8.49], elevation +4.84 [3.11,6.58], and ID −0.2. Orbital interpolation is −4.29 [−7.56,−1.22], with control/SCVC 90.0/85.7.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table II, C1 dolly, C2 elevation, and C3 endpoint rows
evidence.detail: Dolly extrapolation: 99 tasks, 67.0/71.2, +4.24 [0.71,7.88]. Elevation: 386 tasks, 54.9/63.7, +8.76 [6.40,11.11]. Endpoint interpolation/extrapolation differences are −0.97 [−3.71,1.61] and −0.58 [−2.12,1.02].

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table II, ID and C2 azimuth in-distribution rows
evidence.detail: Nominal four-suite success is 92.3% control versus 91.7% SCVC. Distribution-matched azimuth improves from 84.0% to 88.5%, with paired difference +4.52 [2.65,6.39].

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Section VII, 'Where the effect stops, and why'
evidence.detail: Reports primary-extrapolation spatial gains of 40.8 points, object losses of 11.6, and compound-shift object losses of 40.4. Grasp precision versus viewpoint disorientation is offered as an explanatory interpretation.

Limits include exact-pair acquisition, simulated WAM evidence, demonstration-only consistency, one elevation extrapolation point, small high-success interpolation buckets, training-seed variation, scene-only scope, and deferred quantitative shrinkage measurement at full scale.

evidence.location: PDF p. 2, Introduction, final contribution paragraph
evidence.detail: The authors state that code and protocol tooling will be released; this passage does not supply a repository or establish current availability.
